style_guide: Two visual worlds joined by one warm thread of light. MODERN WORLD (scenes 0, 1, 6, 7): photorealistic, cinematic, 35mm/50mm lenses, shallow depth of field, gentle film grain. Night interiors begin in cool desaturated blue (#1B2A41, #3A5A80 screen glow) and resolve to warm tungsten amber (#E8A951, #C97B2E) as calm returns. The person is always anonymous: seen from behind, in silhouette, or as hands only. Generic, unbranded objects only. EPIC WORLD (scenes 2–5): painterly, reverent devotional realism inspired by classical Indian miniature and oil-painting traditions, with soft brushwork and luminous haze. Golden-dawn palette of saffron, ochre, ivory, deep peacock blue (#1F4E79) and Krishna's yellow silk (#F2C14E). Slow, steady camera moves; never shaky. All divine and epic figures appear with dignity in traditional iconography. Krishna is blue-complexioned, wears yellow silk and a crown with a peacock feather, and is serene. Arjuna wears princely warrior attire with the bow Gandiva. Battle armies appear only at a distance, still and non-violent. CONTINUITY: a warm flame or lamp glow links the scenes and grows from tiny to dominant as the story moves from noise to clarity. Mood arc: overwhelmed, then reverent, then honest, then quiet resolve. NO text, letters, logos, watermarks or legible screens in any generated frame; all on-screen text, the verse and the Echoes of Gita title are added in editing. Master aspect 4:5, composed with safe margins so it can be reframed to 9:16 (keep key subjects centred, with headroom at top and bottom for captions).

assets.prompt: Painterly, reverent wide establishing shot of the plain of Kurukshetra at golden dawn, in the style of classical Indian devotional painting with soft oil brushwork. A vast open earthen field rolls under a luminous saffron and ivory sky with low haze. Two great armies stand very far in the distance on either side, tiny, still and softly hazy, with tall cloth banners raised and fluttering gently; there is no combat. In the centre foreground-middle ground stands a magnificent ornate golden chariot drawn by four white horses. Krishna is seated as charioteer at the front and Arjuna stands behind him, both small in frame and shown as dignified silhouettes against the rising sun. Light dust motes drift in the golden air. Very slow aerial drift forward. Palette of ochre, saffron, ivory and soft peacock blue. Mood: vast, solemn, on the edge of decision.

assets.prompt: Warm, calm, gender-neutral adult narrator with a gentle Indian-English accent: intimate, sincere and unhurried, like a trusted friend sharing something meaningful. Scenes 0–1 are slightly quicker and empathetic. Scenes 2–3 are reverent and storytelling. For the verse in scene 4, slow down noticeably, speak with softness and gravity, and leave a short pause before the citation. In scene 5, pronounce 'iva' as 'EE-vuh' and 'Kurukshetra' as 'koo-roo-KSHAY-truh'. Scene 6 is reflective and tender, with brief pauses after 'Pause.' and 'I am confused.' Scene 7 is warm and inviting. Script: Ten tabs open. Ten experts. Ten opposite answers about your life. Even Arjuna knew this feeling. / Take the safe job. Follow your passion. Move abroad. Stay near family. Every voice sounds certain, and you feel less certain than ever. / On the field of Kurukshetra, Arjuna had just heard Krishna speak of steady wisdom, and of action. To him, the two teachings seemed to pull in different directions. / So Arjuna did not pretend to understand. He turned to his teacher and spoke honestly. / With these perplexing words Thou only confusest my understanding; therefore tell me with certainty the one way by which I may reach bliss. Bhagavad Gita, chapter three, verse two. / In the Sanskrit, Arjuna even softens his words with 'iva', meaning 'as if'. He doesn't blame his teacher. He admits his bewilderment and asks for clarity, and that sincere question opens the whole teaching of Karma Yoga. / A reflection, not scripture: perhaps all this noise isn't a personal failure. Perhaps the first step is Arjuna's step. Pause. Admit, 'I am confused.' And turn sincerely to one trusted source of wisdom, rather than collecting ten more voices. / Krishna's answer unfolds across all of Chapter Three. Keep reading with us.

assets.prompt: 52-second instrumental underscore with no vocals. 0–11s (modern overwhelm): a sparse, slightly restless ambient electronic pulse with soft muted piano and subtle ticking textures, building gently in density, then cutting to near-silence at 11s as the phone buzzing fades. 11–25s (Kurukshetra): a low tanpura drone enters with a warm string pad and a distant, noble bansuri melody in a contemplative raga mood such as Yaman or Bhairav; spacious, dawn-like and reverent, never martial. 25–33s (verse): music drops to just the tanpura drone and one sustained soft note, leaving room for the voice. 33–40s (iva): delicate santoor or harp shimmer over the drone. 40–52s (resolution): the warm piano returns, joined by the bansuri in a hopeful, gentle resolution on a major-leaning cadence, ending in a soft fade. Mix sits under narration at about -18 LUFS, with a peaceful, sincere and devotional overall feel.
